They met with Orlanthi who follow a tribal king named Arim. Arim is married to a great earth magician named Sorana the Priestess, or Sorana Tor. Like us, Arim and his people came to Dragon Pass after an invader conquered their homeland. In their case, the homeland was to the north, and their conquerors were the Chaotic Red Empire.

The customs of these Tarshites were different from ours, but they still knew the most important Orlanthi laws.

Ovartien was a popular king; he mounted frequent raids against the part of the Lunar Empire called Sylila, thus enriching his people. He allied with our hated foes, the Horse-Spawn, who they called Grazers. The Horse-Spawn helped them on their raids against the Lunars.

Now Ovartien faces a war with his former Horse-Spawn allies, a war not of his making. Ovartien’s son, Yarandros, has stolen some of the Horse-Spawn breeding stock, the best and most magical of their terrible leaping beasts. Now the horse nomads make war on the Tarshites. Some of the people blame Ovartien for not reining in his steed-mad son, but others support the hot-blooded young man. I say it is good that our Horse-Spawn enemies are drawn to fight someone else for a change.

Our explorers heard that Yarandros, son of Ovartien Twinson, was the new king of Tarsh. After Yarandros had provoked war with Ovartien’s Horse-Spawn allies, Ovartien abdicated his throne in protest. Yarandros’ ascent to the throne had been controversial, for his supporters said that both his qualifications and his bloodline ought to make him king. Our explorers found spirits at Mount Kero Fin, who claimed kinship with Orlanth. Helganna the Knowing said we should sacrifice to them.
